title: Quiet-window orchestration and multi-touch status flow
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This document defines the Quiet-Window Orchestration pattern used by Redwood’s on-call teams to coordinate low-noise restorations and staggered customer communications for partial degradations. It focuses on: when to enter a quiet window, who owns the bridge and outbound messages, how to schedule multi-touch status updates, and templates for status-page and customer notices. The goal is to minimize unnecessary churn for customers while keeping transparency and regulatory evidence intact.

Scope

- Applies to incidents classified as: Partial-degradation (P2/P3), Rate-limited latency blips, KV-cache warmup issues, and dependency throttles that are actively being mitigated and have no immediate data-loss implications.
- Not intended for: full-region outages, security incidents, or incidents requiring immediate public full-page status (see escalation matrix for those flows).

Activation criteria (quick reference)

1) SLO impact below outage threshold (e.g., 99.97% availability still met).
2) Active remediation in progress with clear owner and ETA <= 6 hours.
3) No ongoing customer-facing data loss or compromised integrity.
4) Customer-impact tier = limited subset (<= 5% of tenants) or feature-specific.

Bridge owner and primary roles

- Bridge Operator (primary): opens/maintains the incident bridge, sets quiet window timer, coordinates triage tasks.
- Incident Lead (secondary): owns technical decisions and rollout plan.
- Communications Lead: drafts status page entries and customer comms, approves cadence.
- Support Liaison: aggregates affected customer list and CS updates.

Bridge operator checklist (ordered runbook)

1) Open bridge and set purpose line: "QUIET-WINDOW: partial-degradation; low-noise updates; ETA < 6h". Include JIRA/INC ticket.
2) Confirm incident classification and affected scope (service names, regions, model variants).
3) Assign remediation owner(s) and set target milestones (investigate, mitigate, verify).
4) If criteria met, toggle quiet window mode (see #Toggle procedure).
5) Schedule multi-touch status updates (initial, confirmation, resolution) and assign owners for each tick.
6) If customers escalate or SLA customers impacted, escalate to public status and exit quiet window.

Toggle procedure (explicit steps)

- Enter quiet window:
  1. Incident Lead confirms criteria.
  2. Bridge Operator updates bridge topic and Confluence incident page.
  3. Communications Lead sets status-page visibility to "limited internal" (internal-flag:quiet-window).
  4. Support Liaison adds affected customer list and watchlist to the bridge.

- Exit quiet window (fast path):
  1. Any time a P1 triggers or customer escalation occurs, Incident Lead signals exit.
  2. Communications Lead pushes immediate public status page message and customer email.

Multi-touch status cadence (recommended)

- Touch 0 (T0) — Acknowledgement (0–15 minutes): internal-only bridge summary, high-level impact.
- Touch 1 (T1) — Confirmation (30–60 minutes): concise internal update for stakeholders; still quiet to customers.
- Touch 2 (T2) — Customer notification (2–3 hours): targeted messages to affected customers (limited list), short explanation, ETA or next check-in time.
- Touch 3 (T3) — Resolution (on fix): public status page entry + per-customer follow-up as needed.

Status page message templates

- Internal acknowledgement (T0):
  Title: "Investigating elevated latency for [service] (partial, limited scope)"
  Body: "We are investigating elevated latency observed in <region>. Impact is limited to a subset of customers using <feature>. No data loss detected. Bridge: <bridge-link>. Next update: 30–60m."

- Targeted customer notice (T2):
  Subject: "Status update: degraded performance for <feature> — <region>"
  Body: "Hello — We are currently addressing degraded performance for <feature> that may affect a subset of requests originating in <region>. Our engineers have identified the likely root cause and are rolling a mitigation. Expected next update: <ETA or time window>. If you need immediate assistance, reply to this thread or open a support ticket: <ticket-link>."

- Public resolution (T3):
  Title: "Resolved: performance degradation for <service> in <region>"
  Body: "We resolved a partial degradation affecting <feature>. Root cause: <short cause>. Remediation: <actions taken>. If you observe lingering issues, contact support with the incident id <INC-ID>."

Customer comms escalation matrix (condensed)

| Trigger | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| >= 1 SLA customer reports impact | Send immediate targeted email + offer 1:1 call | Support Liaison |
| >5% tenants impacted or public complaints trending | Promote to public status page and send broad notification | Communications Lead |
| Security or data integrity issue | Follow security incident playbook (restricted) | Security Team (pager) |

On-call rotation guidance and cadence alignment

- Recommended rotation: primary on-call 1 week, secondary 2 weeks. Primary owns initial bridge and day-to-day quiet window maintenance; secondary provides backup and weekend cross-over.
- Handoff checklist (end of shift): latest incident state, pending tasks, next check-in times, and any scheduled customer messages. Use the standardized Handoff form: Incident ID, Next ETA, Outstanding Actions.

Game-day exercises (focused scenarios)

1) KV-cache cold-start storm — objective: practice quiet-window entry and staggered customer comms while KV-cache warms.
2) Noisy neighbor GPU contention — objective: capacity triage, schedule throttling messaging, and validate SLA customer escalation path.
3) Targeted model-quality regression — objective: coordinate serving rollback (canary), manage quiet-window while validating outputs.

Each game-day should include:
- A pre-brief with success criteria.
- A simulated support queue with 3 escalations (2 routine, 1 SLA).
- Post-run scoring: Time-to-first-fix, Time-to-customer-notice, and customer satisfaction (simulated response).

Postmortem & evidence collection requirements

- Use the standard postmortem template and attach: timestamped logs, bridge-recording (if any), status-page messages, per-customer tickets, and the quiet-window decision rationale.
- If quiet window was used, include a short blameless justification section: why quiet window was chosen, alternative options considered, and lessons learned about communication cadence.

Operational thresholds and quick-reference table

| Metric | Quiet-window allowed? | Action threshold |
|---|---:|---|
| SLO degradation < 0.1% | Yes | Maintain quiet window, update T1 every 60m |
| SLO degradation >= 0.5% | No | Promote to public status and escalate to P1 flow |
| > 5% tenants affected | No | Promote to public status, initiate external comms |
| Any data loss | No | Exit quiet window; follow data-loss playbook |

Ownership and escalation contacts (short)

- Incident Lead: oncall-primary@redwood.ai
- Bridge Operator: bridge-ops@redwood.ai
- Communications Lead: comms@redwood.ai
- Support Liaison: enterprise-support@redwood.ai
- Security Pager: +1-555-SEC-0001 (restricted)

Appendix: sample CLI snippets and Confluence macros

- Toggle quiet-window label on incident page (example):
  curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood.ai/incidents/<INC-ID>/labels" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"labels":["quiet-window"]}'

- Example status-page payload (minimal):
  {
    "status": "investigating",
    "component": "text-generation:us-west",
    "message": "Partial degradation affecting a subset of requests; targeted customers notified."
  }

- Bridge naming convention: QW-YYYYMMDD-<service>-<short-desc> (e.g., QW-20260207-serve-kv-cache-warm)

Review cadence and document lifecycle

- This doc is reviewed quarterly by eng-sre and oncall ops. Major incidents that used the quiet-window pattern must append their incident review to the related pages list within five business days.

Related artifacts

- Incident evidence checklist (link): /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-evidence-chain-and-forensic-runbook-2025
- Postmortem template (link): /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026

If you have questions about applying quiet-window patterns to a specific customer contract or if an external regulator requires different communications, contact Legal or Security before sending customer-facing messages.
